subject: baby skeleton x-ray
title: You Were Born With About 300 Bones. Now You Have 206

scenes.text: You've lost about 100 bones since you were born. None of them fell out.
Babies are born with around 300 bones. Adults have 206.
A newborn's skull alone starts as 44 separate pieces, held together by six soft spots.
Within the first year or so, bone fills those soft spots in.
Your upper arm starts as three or four separate bits. They join up after about three years.
The last to finish is your collarbone, in your early to mid twenties. So the count might still be going.

description:
You were born with around 300 bones; adults have 206, because many of them fuse as you grow.
A newborn's skull starts as 44 separate elements joined by six fontanelles, which bone replaces in the first year or so. The upper arm begins as three or four pieces that meet after about three years. Most fusing is done around puberty, but the collarbone isn't fully formed until the early to mid twenties.
Did you know babies have more bones than you?
first_comment: Your skull went from 44 pieces to just over 20. Which bone do you think fuses last?
